tested_scope: One bounded documented/read-only GitHub repository-identity leaf: current repository metadata plus official GitHub documentation for Get a repository, global node IDs, and delete/restore behavior; six constructed histories covering prior-incarnation witness present/lost, effect binding present/absent, delete/recreate, and same-incarnation content rollback. No destructive delete/recreate experiment was performed.

documented_api_surface: GitHub REST 'Get a repository' returns both numeric id and node_id for a repository object.
GitHub documents node_id as a global node ID that identifies an object and can be persisted for later object lookup across REST/GraphQL API use.

GitHub documents that repositories can be deleted and some deleted repositories can be restored within 90 days, but the bounded documentation inspected here does not specify a monotonic repository-generation contract or whether id/node_id is guaranteed to change or remain unchanged across every delete/restore/recreate path.

constructed_histories.history: Old repository incarnation I1 produced an effect proposal bound to node_id I1; owner/name is later recreated as I2 and current read returns I2.
constructed_histories.result: Current-incarnation comparison rejects the I1-bound proposal before a repository-authoritative effect. Narrow stale cross-incarnation replay fence succeeds.

constructed_histories.history: Old incarnation I1 is recorded in a trusted role-local predecessor witness; current read returns different I2, but the pending proposal itself lacks an incarnation binding.
constructed_histories.result: The worker can detect that repository incarnation changed and fail closed, but cannot safely attribute the unbound proposal to the new incarnation.

constructed_histories.history: Prior witness is lost with repository deletion/rollback, but the stale proposal still carries old node_id I1 and current read returns I2.
constructed_histories.result: Proposal binding alone detects the cross-incarnation stale replay.

constructed_histories.history: Prior witness is lost/rolled back and a stale proposal carries no prior repository identity; current read returns only current I2.
constructed_histories.result: Current identity alone has no historical comparator. Accepting the proposal would be unproven; safety requires fail-closed or another monotonic witness.

constructed_histories.history: Repository contents roll back while the currently observed repository object identity does not provide a documented changed-generation signal.
constructed_histories.result: Current repository id/node_id is an object discriminator, not a documented content-generation counter; same-incarnation content rollback remains undetected by identity alone.

constructed_histories.history: Two current projections have the same owner/name, same visible contents and the same currently observed repository identity: one history is legitimate current state, the other includes an earlier deleted/rolled-back history whose witness is no longer present.
constructed_histories.result: With no trusted predecessor identity or effect binding outside the lost state, the current read-only projection does not prove the absent history never occurred. Standalone historical freshness is therefore not established.

result.new_positive_evidence: Repository id/node_id is useful as a current-incarnation discriminator. Binding each role-authored claim/effect proposal to the observed repository node_id and checking the current node_id at the repository-authoritative write boundary fences stale proposals from a different known incarnation in the constructed C1/C3 cases without hosted coordination.
result.new_falsification: Repository identity is not, by itself, a rollback-proof monotonic freshness floor. If both the trusted prior-incarnation witness and the proposal's prior-incarnation binding are absent because they lived in the deleted/rolled-back repository state, the current id/node_id supplies no historical comparison; the bounded GitHub documentation also does not promise generation monotonicity across every delete/restore/recreate path.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: A sink-side or otherwise rollback-domain-independent minimum-generation/freshness witness that survives repository deletion/recreate and can reject stale generations without richer-mode/protected/manual execution, external hosted coordination, or finite monthly/trial/paid quota.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport_rate_limit_dependen: bounded GitHub metadata/contents transport only; rate-limit interruption remains checkpoint/fail-closed behavior and is not used as compute

scope_guard: Do not generalize the narrow repository-incarnation fence to arbitrary sinks, undocumented GitHub restore identity semantics, same-incarnation content rollback, or histories where no trusted old identity survives. No claim is made that GitHub guarantees node_id change on every recreate/restore path.
continuation: Part101: execute exactly one bounded sink-side minimum-generation leaf. Model a stale proposal carrying {repository_node_id, generation, effect_id} against a current repository incarnation after delete/recreate and test whether any Chat-native authoritative sink available without protected/admin setup can atomically reject generation below a durable minimum while preserving idempotent retry. Compare (a) repository-only CAS/current-node check, (b) durable sink-local minimum-generation state, and (c) missing/rolled-back sink floor. If no rollback-domain-independent sink floor exists without external hosted coordination or manual/protected setup, preserve that as the unresolved child rather than treating repository identity as sufficient.
